open_points.subject: deferred staff email flows
open_points.text: Status says account creation, email change, and password reset "complete through single-use purpose-bound challenges" and security changes "produce notifications"; State 0 R0-23 says those challenge operations and notices are inert and read, write, audit, and deliver nothing.
open_points.question: Are challenge records, delivery records, challenge consumption, and security notifications part of the accepted product now, or only a future design?
options: Accepted service: all challenge and notification operations remain inert and create no records
Former design: challenges are issued and consumed and notifications are delivered
open_points.default_guess: Treat them as future-only and keep the accepted service inert.

witness.initial: An administrator has created a pending staff account.
events: The administrator attempts to issue email verification.
The holder attempts to consume the received token.
outcomes: No challenge or delivery is created; both operations follow R0-23 and the account remains pending until administrator activation.
A challenge and delivery are created; consuming it verifies the email and activates the account.

open_points.subject: secret plaintext lifetime
open_points.text: "plaintext exists only in the issuing response" conflicts with staff passwords being supplied in login, account-creation, password-change, and reset-completion requests, and with session/access secrets being presented on authenticated requests.
open_points.question: In which inbound and outbound product actions may each secret exist transiently in plaintext?
options: Plaintext may exist transiently both when issued and when later presented for verification
Plaintext is permitted only in issuing responses, making the described authentication and password commands impossible as written
open_points.default_guess: Allow plaintext transiently in issuing responses and authenticated/presentation inputs, but never persist or log it.

witness.initial: An active staff account has a stored password hash.
events: The holder submits a login request containing the password.
outcomes: The service transiently handles plaintext to verify it.
The modeling convention rejects any plaintext outside an issuing response, so login cannot be implemented as described.

open_points.subject: ClientViewer management authority
open_points.text: "Created/modified by: operator or administrator only" conflicts with State 0 R0-14, which makes creation, revocation, and re-issuing of client viewers administrator-only.
open_points.question: Can an operator create, modify, or revoke a ClientViewer?
options: Only an administrator can manage ClientViewer records
Operators and administrators can manage ClientViewer records
open_points.default_guess: Restrict all ClientViewer management to administrators.

witness.initial: An active operator has an assigned active project but no access-management capability.
events: The operator submits a request to create a viewer.
outcomes: The request is denied under R0-14.
A ClientViewer is created under M01.

open_points.subject: viewer display-name mutation
open_points.text: The model says "Created/modified by" but identifies only creation and terminal revocation; it does not say whether `display_name` can be changed or which action changes it.
open_points.question: Is `display_name` mutable after viewer creation?
options: An administrator may rename the viewer without changing identity
The display name is immutable; the only later mutation is revocation
open_points.default_guess: Allow an administrator to rename the viewer while retaining `viewer_id`.

witness.initial: An active viewer has display name "Ana Gómez" and active grants.
events: An administrator tries to correct the display name to "Ana García".
outcomes: The existing ClientViewer is updated and all grants continue to name it.
The correction is refused because no rename lifecycle action exists.
witness.observer: The administrator and staff viewing the client list

open_points.subject: viewer credential management authority
open_points.text: "Created/modified by: operator or administrator" conflicts with State 0 R0-14, which reserves creation, revocation, and re-issuing of viewer access links to administrators.
open_points.question: Can an operator issue, re-issue, or revoke a ViewerAccessCredential?
options: Only administrators can manage viewer credentials
Operators and administrators can manage viewer credentials
open_points.default_guess: Restrict credential management to administrators.

witness.initial: A viewer has one live access credential; an operator lacks access-management capability.
events: The operator requests a replacement access link.
outcomes: The request is denied and the old credential remains valid.
A new credential is minted and the old credential and sessions are revoked.

open_points.subject: staff authority to revoke viewer sessions
open_points.text: ViewerSession says it is revoked by "explicit staff action" while State 0 R0-14 makes access revocation administrator-only.
open_points.question: Does "staff" here mean any operator or only an administrator with access-management capability?
options: Only an administrator may explicitly revoke viewer sessions
Any operator or administrator may explicitly revoke viewer sessions
open_points.default_guess: Require an administrator with access-management capability.

witness.initial: A viewer has an active session and an operator has access only to one project.
events: The operator explicitly revokes the viewer session.
outcomes: Revocation is denied because the operator lacks access-management capability.
The session is revoked because M03 permits an explicit staff action.

open_points.subject: viewer-grant management authority
open_points.text: "Created/modified by: operator or administrator" conflicts with State 0 R0-14, which makes viewer project grants administrator-only.
open_points.question: Can an operator create or revoke a ProjectViewerGrant?
options: Only administrators may create or revoke grants
Operators and administrators may create or revoke grants
open_points.default_guess: Restrict grant management to administrators.

witness.initial: An operator is assigned to active project P and viewer V has no grant to P.
events: The operator attempts to grant V access to P.
outcomes: The request is denied under R0-14.
An active ProjectViewerGrant is created under M04.

open_points.subject: re-grant after revocation
open_points.text: The lifecycle is `active → revoked`, while the rule only says "at most one active grant" and does not say whether access can later be granted again, whether the revoked record is reactivated, or whether a new grant is minted.
open_points.question: After revocation, can the same viewer be granted the same project again, and if so what is the identity of that grant?
options: Mint a new ProjectViewerGrant; the revoked grant remains history
Reactivate the existing grant
Revocation permanently forbids that viewer/project pair
open_points.default_guess: Mint a new grant and retain the revoked one.

witness.initial: Viewer V previously had grant G to active project P; G is revoked.
events: An administrator grants V access to P again.
outcomes: A fresh grant G2 is created and G remains revoked.
The operation reactivates G or is refused because its lifecycle is terminal.
witness.observer: The administrator, viewer, and audit reader

open_points.subject: staff activation and email verification
open_points.text: M05 says the lifecycle is `pending_verification → active` and that the login email changes only through challenge-based models, but does not name administrator activation; its surrounding former design makes challenge consumption the activation path. State 0 R0-19 instead says an administrator activates the account and that activation marks the email verified while challenges are deferred.
open_points.question: Which product action moves a pending staff account to active and sets `email_verified_at` in the accepted service?
options: Administrator status activation atomically marks the email verified
Consumption of an EmailVerificationChallenge activates the account
Either action can activate it
open_points.default_guess: Use administrator activation only while challenges are deferred.

witness.initial: A newly created account is pending with `email_verified_at = null`.
events: An administrator invokes the accepted status-activation action.
outcomes: The account becomes active and verified under R0-19.
The account cannot become active until an email challenge is consumed.

open_points.subject: self-service password change
open_points.text: "Created/modified by: administrator" conflicts with State 0 R0-19, where the holder logs in and changes the initial password through `change_staff_password`.
open_points.question: May an authenticated staff holder change their own `password_hash`, and what account/session effects does that action have?
options: The holder may change their own password
Only an administrator may modify the account password
open_points.default_guess: Allow an authenticated holder to change their own password.

witness.initial: An administrator has activated an account with an initial password, and its holder has logged in.
events: The holder submits a password change.
outcomes: The account's password hash changes under R0-19.
The change is denied because M05 allows only administrator modification.

open_points.subject: role changes after creation
open_points.text: `role` is a persisted field and administrators may modify the account, but no action or lifecycle rule says whether an existing account can move between `operator` and `administrator`.
open_points.question: Can an administrator change an existing StaffAccount's role after creation?
options: Role is mutable between operator and administrator
Role is fixed at account creation
open_points.default_guess: Permit an audited administrator-only role change.

witness.initial: An active operator account exists.
events: An administrator attempts to promote it to administrator.
outcomes: The same StaffAccount becomes an administrator and immediately receives the static administrator capabilities.
The action is unavailable because role is immutable.
witness.observer: The promoted staff member and other administrators

open_points.subject: assignment target role
open_points.text: The purpose says "explicit operator scope" but the field is `staff_id` and no rule says that the referenced StaffAccount must currently have role `operator`.
open_points.question: May an assignment be created for an administrator, and what happens to assignments when an operator's role changes?
options: Assignments are valid only for operator-role accounts
Assignments may reference any StaffAccount but are ignored for administrators
Assignments scope administrators too
open_points.default_guess: Allow records only for operators; preserve but ignore them if the account becomes administrator.

witness.initial: Staff account S is an administrator in the single administrative area.
events: An administrator attempts to create an assignment from S to project P.
outcomes: Creation is refused because administrators derive scope from area policy.
An active assignment is created because the schema accepts any `staff_id`.

open_points.subject: reassignment after revocation
open_points.text: The assignment lifecycle is `active → revoked`, but "at most one active assignment" does not say whether a revoked staff/project pair may be assigned again or whether that uses a new identity.
open_points.question: After an assignment is revoked, can the operator later be assigned to the same project again, and is a new assignment minted?
options: Create a new assignment and retain the revoked record
Reactivate the old assignment
Revocation permanently prevents reassignment
open_points.default_guess: Create a new assignment.

witness.initial: Operator S has revoked assignment A to active project P.
events: An administrator assigns S to P again.
outcomes: A new assignment A2 is created.
A is reactivated or the request is refused.
witness.observer: The operator, administrator, and audit reader

open_points.subject: password-reset token creation
open_points.text: M08 says reset tokens are created by self-service request or administrator, delivered through email, consumed, and revoke sessions; State 0 R0-23 says reset requests do nothing and reset completion reads, writes, audits, and delivers nothing.
open_points.question: Can any accepted-service product action currently create or consume a PasswordResetToken?
options: No; M08 is future-only while the feature is deferred
Yes; self-service or administrators can issue and consume reset tokens
open_points.default_guess: Create no PasswordResetToken until the deferred feature is implemented.

witness.initial: An active verified staff account exists.
events: The holder requests a password reset.
outcomes: The response is concealed but no token, delivery, or audit record is created.
A PasswordResetToken and delivery are created.

open_points.subject: email-verification challenge lifecycle
open_points.text: M09 says a challenge is created at account creation or re-issue and consuming it activates the account; State 0 R0-19 and R0-23 say creation/confirmation are inert and administrator activation performs verification.
open_points.question: Is EmailVerificationChallenge instantiated and consumed in the accepted service?
options: No; administrator activation verifies the email without a challenge
Yes; challenge consumption verifies and activates the account
open_points.default_guess: Treat M09 as an unimplemented future model and use administrator activation.

witness.initial: An administrator creates a staff account.
events: Account creation completes.
The holder attempts email confirmation.
outcomes: No challenge exists; confirmation is concealed rejection and administrator activation is required.
A challenge exists and confirmation activates the account.

open_points.subject: ordinary email-change lifecycle
open_points.text: M10 says staff or an administrator creates a pending change and consumption changes the login email; State 0 R0-23 says requesting and confirming email changes do nothing, while R0-20 defines only the separate recovery override as an implemented direct replacement.
open_points.question: Can any ordinary product action currently create or consume PendingEmailChange?
options: No; ordinary email change is deferred and only recovery override changes email
Yes; staff or administrators can stage and consume email changes
open_points.default_guess: Keep ordinary email change inert and reserve direct replacement for the recovery override.

witness.initial: An active staff account uses old@example.test.
events: The holder requests a change to new@example.test.
The holder attempts confirmation.
outcomes: No PendingEmailChange is created and the old email remains.
A PendingEmailChange is created and consumption replaces the login email.

open_points.subject: email-delivery record creation
open_points.text: M11 says it is "Created by: the email challenge/notification flow" and modified by a gateway-result handler; State 0 R0-23 says those flows deliver and write nothing and no token-free notice is sent.
open_points.question: Are EmailDeliveryRecord instances created by any accepted-service action now?
options: No; the model is dormant until email features are implemented
Yes; challenge and notification actions create delivery records
open_points.default_guess: Create no delivery records while all email flows are deferred.

witness.initial: An administrator suspends an active staff account.
events: The suspension commits.
outcomes: No security notice or EmailDeliveryRecord is created.
An account-security delivery record is created and sent to the gateway.

open_points.subject: email gateway invocation
open_points.text: M12 says the DTO is consumed by `email_delivery_gateway`; State 0 says the gateway is called by no operation of the running portal.
open_points.question: Can the accepted service currently create and send an EmailDeliveryRequest?
options: No; it is a future-only DTO
Yes; implemented challenge or notification flows send it
open_points.default_guess: Do not create or send this DTO until email delivery is implemented.

witness.initial: A password-change action succeeds.
events: The owning flow reaches its notification step.
outcomes: No request is created and the gateway is not called.
An EmailDeliveryRequest for `password_changed_notice` is sent.
witness.observer: The gateway operator and staff holder

open_points.subject: all-project producer authority
open_points.text: M13 says `scope_mode = all_projects` is an administrator decision and capabilities are static per source type; State 0 says "a global producer exists only through an explicitly granted capability."
open_points.question: Does `all_projects` alone authorize publication to every project, or is a distinct global capability/grant also required?
options: The audited `all_projects` scope mode is sufficient
A separate explicitly granted global capability is required in addition to scope mode
open_points.default_guess: Treat the explicitly selected and audited `all_projects` scope as the global grant.

witness.initial: An active estimate producer has `scope_mode = all_projects`, no project grant, and the static import capability.
events: It imports a snapshot for active project P.
outcomes: The import passes project scope because `all_projects` is sufficient.
The import is scope-denied because no explicit global capability/grant exists.

open_points.subject: scope-mode mutation
open_points.text: M13 says the principal is "Created/modified by" an administrator but does not say whether `scope_mode` may change after creation or what happens to existing ProducerProjectGrant records when it does.
open_points.question: Can an administrator switch an existing principal between `granted_projects` and `all_projects`, and how do existing grants behave?
options: Scope mode is mutable and grants are retained for possible later reuse
Scope mode is immutable after principal creation
Changing scope mode revokes or deletes existing grants
open_points.default_guess: Allow an audited mode change and retain grant history without treating grants as active authority in `all_projects` mode.

witness.initial: Producer S uses `granted_projects` and has an active grant only to P1.
events: An administrator changes S to `all_projects`.
Later the administrator changes S back to `granted_projects`.
outcomes: The old P1 grant is retained and becomes effective again.
The first change is forbidden, or the old grant is removed and P1 is no longer authorized after switching back.

open_points.subject: producer re-grant after revocation
open_points.text: The model has an `active | revoked` status and at most one active grant per pair, but does not state whether the same principal/project pair can be granted again after revocation or which grant identity is used.
open_points.question: Can a revoked producer/project scope later be restored, and if so by creating a new grant or reactivating the old one?
options: Create a new grant and preserve the revoked record
Reactivate the old grant
Revocation permanently forbids the pair
open_points.default_guess: Create a new ProducerProjectGrant.

witness.initial: Producer S has revoked grant G to active project P and uses `granted_projects`.
events: An administrator grants S access to P again.
outcomes: A fresh grant G2 is minted.
G is reactivated or the request is refused.
witness.observer: The administrator, producer, and audit reader

open_points.subject: snapshot entity identity
open_points.text: The model has a portal-generated `snapshot_id`, but its explicit identity is "unique `(project_id, estimate_id, estimate_version)`" and its identity evidence says snapshots are addressed by that tuple.
open_points.question: Is the entity's canonical identity `snapshot_id`, the producer-owned tuple, or a composite in which the tuple is only a uniqueness key?
options: `snapshot_id` is the entity ID and the tuple is an immutable alternate key
The tuple is the entity identity and `snapshot_id` is only an internal reference
Both are public identities with defined equivalence
open_points.default_guess: Use `snapshot_id` as the portal entity ID and enforce the tuple as an immutable unique business key.

witness.initial: An accepted snapshot has tuple T and portal UUID S.
events: A budget version references the snapshot.
A producer republishes tuple T identically.
outcomes: All portal references use S; tuple T resolves to that entity as an alternate key.
The tuple itself is the identity and consumers need not preserve or expose S.
witness.observer: Budget modules, producer-result readers, and audit readers

open_points.subject: integrity-conflict reject reason
open_points.text: `reject_reason` is required when outcome is `integrity_conflict`, but the closed `ImportRejectReason` catalog contains no integrity-conflict member.
open_points.question: What fact is stored in `reject_reason` for an integrity-conflict import record?
options: Add a dedicated integrity-conflict reason
Set no reason for `integrity_conflict` and narrow the conditional requirement to `rejected`
Reuse one of the listed rejection reasons despite its different meaning
open_points.default_guess: Add a dedicated integrity-conflict reason.

witness.initial: Snapshot tuple T is already stored with fingerprint F1.
events: The same producer republishes T with fingerprint F2.
outcomes: A new import record cannot satisfy its required closed reason field.
An implementer invents or reuses a reason value, producing a different model fact from another implementation.
witness.observer: The producer reading the import result and audit readers

open_points.subject: PortalSection deletion
open_points.text: "a section is never deleted while any allocation or progress record references it" states only the forbidden case and leaves open whether an unreferenced section can be deleted, retired, or must exist forever.
open_points.question: What lifecycle applies when a PortalSection has no allocations or progress references and no current plan?
options: It may be deleted by a defined budget-management action
It is never deleted and remains historical identity
It becomes explicitly retired/inactive
open_points.default_guess: Retain it permanently unless a later explicit retirement model is introduced.

witness.initial: A manual section has no allocations or progress and its plan is removed from the manual budget.
events: An administrator or operator removes the section from the budget.
outcomes: The PortalSection record is deleted because it is unreferenced.
The PortalSection remains as historical identity even though no plan uses it.

open_points.subject: source-key namespace
open_points.text: `source_key` is only the producer's `source_section_id` and is unique per project, but the texts do not state whether that source ID is globally stable across source systems, estimates, and producers for the project.
open_points.question: What namespace makes an imported `source_section_id` safe as a project-wide PortalSection correspondence key?
options: The ID is guaranteed unique and stable across every producer and estimate for a project
The key must include source system or estimate identity
Automatic linking is allowed only within a specified estimate lineage
open_points.default_guess: Namespace the key by source system and stable estimate lineage unless the inbound contract guarantees project-wide uniqueness.

witness.initial: Project P has an accepted snapshot from producer A whose section ID is `1`, linked to section S.
events: Producer B imports another approved estimate for P with an unrelated section also identified as `1`.
Staff activates the new version.
outcomes: The new plan reuses S because `source_key` is project-wide.
A distinct PortalSection is created because producer/estimate namespace is part of correspondence.
witness.observer: The client and staff viewing allocations and progress

open_points.subject: reactivation of a deactivated budget version
open_points.text: The lifecycle is `inactive → active → inactive`; it does not state whether the final inactive state may transition to active again.
open_points.question: May staff reactivate a previously active and deactivated BudgetVersion?
options: Yes; any inactive retained version may be activated again
No; once deactivated, a version is historical and terminal
Only never-before-active inactive versions may be activated
open_points.default_guess: Allow reactivation of any retained version if section-linking and allocation rules are applied again.

witness.initial: Version A was active, then activation of B deactivated A.
events: Staff attempts to activate A again.
outcomes: A becomes active and B is deactivated.
The action is refused because A's post-active inactive state is terminal.

open_points.subject: manual section-plan creation and removal
open_points.text: M23 defines editing an existing manual plan but does not state how manual plans are added or removed even though State 0 says an operator maintains ordered manual budget sections.
open_points.question: Which product actions create and remove manual SectionPlan records, and what happens to the related PortalSection?
options: Staff may add and remove manual plans; PortalSection retention follows an explicit rule
Manual plans may be added but never removed
The sole manual version and its complete plan set are created once and only field edits are allowed
open_points.default_guess: Allow staff to add and remove plans on the active-project manual version while retaining referenced PortalSections.

witness.initial: An active project's manual budget has sections Kitchen and Bathroom.
events: The operator adds Electrical and removes unused Bathroom.
outcomes: A new SectionPlan is created and the Bathroom plan is removed under defined lifecycle actions.
Only existing plan values can be edited, so neither structural change is possible.

open_points.subject: manual mapping during imported-version activation
open_points.text: State 0 says sections without stable correspondence "require manual mapping" and existing allocations require explicit mapping; State 1 says unmatched source sections automatically create new PortalSection records and allocations to absent old sections merely become unresolved and must be re-allocated.
open_points.question: Can staff explicitly map an unmatched incoming section to an existing PortalSection during activation, or is re-allocation after automatic creation the only remedy?
options: Activation accepts explicit section-correspondence decisions and reuses the selected PortalSection
Every unmatched incoming section creates a new PortalSection; staff must later replace allocations
Activation is blocked until every unmatched section is mapped
open_points.default_guess: Allow explicit mapping during activation, with automatic creation only for incoming sections deliberately left as new identities.

witness.initial: Old version has PortalSection S with allocations; a new snapshot represents the same real section under a new stable source ID, so automatic key matching fails.
events: Staff reviews and activates the new version.
outcomes: Staff maps the incoming source section to S and existing allocations remain resolved.
Activation creates new section S2 and the old allocations become unresolved until individually re-allocated.
witness.observer: Staff and the client viewing allocation resolution

open_points.subject: authority for recognition publication facts
open_points.text: M25 names the external OCR service as source of truth, while State 0 R0-17 says the portal does not independently verify OCR origin, OCR has no portal principal, and the authenticated staff submission is trusted; the intake interface and OCR "decide nothing."
open_points.question: Which actor is authoritative for submitting the publication and its project/allocation-independent facts to the portal?
options: Authenticated staff is the product authority and OCR provenance is unverified supplied evidence
The external OCR service is the authoritative publisher
An authenticated adapter principal is required, despite State 0 saying none exists
open_points.default_guess: Treat authenticated staff as the accepted-service submitter and preserve OCR identifiers/provenance as unverified external facts.

witness.initial: An authenticated operator possesses a structurally valid confirmed-recognition payload and provenance reference.
events: The operator submits it without any independently authenticated OCR call.
outcomes: The portal accepts it because R0-17 trusts the staff submission.
The portal refuses it because M25 requires the external OCR service as source of truth.

open_points.subject: allocation identity during re-allocation
open_points.text: Identity evidence says allocations are "replaced and audited by id," continuity says "An allocation stays the same record while it is re-allocated," and the lifecycle says "created and replaced."
open_points.question: When staff re-allocates an expense, are existing ExpenseAllocation entities updated in place, deleted and replaced with new identities, or retained as superseded history?
options: Update existing allocation identities where possible and create/delete only for cardinality changes
Replace the complete allocation set with newly minted entities
Retain old allocations as superseded records and mint current ones
open_points.default_guess: Replace the committed current set atomically with new allocation identities and rely on audit for history.

witness.initial: Expense E has allocation A assigning EUR 100 to section S1.
events: An operator reallocates the EUR 100 to S2.
outcomes: A remains the same entity and its target changes to S2.
A is removed or superseded and a new allocation B is minted for S2.
witness.observer: Staff, audit readers, and clients receiving allocation IDs

open_points.subject: progress update eligibility
open_points.text: The model says only sections with planned work in the active version participate in derived progress, but does not say whether staff may create or update SectionProgress for a section absent from the active version or having zero planned work.
open_points.question: Which PortalSections are valid targets of the progress-update action?
options: Only sections present in the active version with positive planned work
Any section present in the active version
Any PortalSection in the project, even if absent from the active budget
open_points.default_guess: Permit updates only for sections present in the active version with positive planned work.

witness.initial: Section S retains historical identity and progress but is absent from the active budget version.
events: An operator submits a new completion percentage for S.
outcomes: The update is rejected because S is not an active planned-work section.
The stored SectionProgress is updated, although it remains excluded from derived progress.
witness.observer: The operator and later readers if S returns in another version

open_points.subject: payment identity minting
open_points.text: The modeling convention says portal-owned UUID identifiers are generated by the portal, but M33 says `payment_id` is a "client-generated idempotency identity, supplied by the operator command."
open_points.question: Who mints a WorkPayment's `payment_id`?
options: The caller generates and supplies it as the stable idempotency identity
The portal generates it and a separate caller idempotency key is needed
The portal generates it on first submission and the caller reuses the returned ID
open_points.default_guess: Keep the explicit M33 rule: the caller supplies the UUID as payment identity.

witness.initial: No payment exists for a EUR 500 transfer.
events: An operator registers the payment without a `payment_id`.
outcomes: The command is invalid because the caller must mint the identity.
The portal accepts it and generates a new payment UUID under the modeling convention.

open_points.subject: authority for photo publication fields
open_points.text: M34 calls this an "input DTO from Telegram intake" and includes `project_id`, section, caption, and visibility, while State 0 R0-17 says the intake interface decides nothing and authenticated staff supplies project selection and publishes the photo.
open_points.question: Which fields come from prepared intake facts and which are authoritative choices of authenticated staff?
options: Intake supplies only stable source/file facts; staff supplies project, section, caption, and visibility
Telegram intake supplies all listed fields and staff merely authorizes them
Staff may override intake-supplied project and presentation fields
open_points.default_guess: Treat `intake_id`, `file_ref`, `photo_date`, and source as intake facts, and project/section/caption/visibility as authenticated staff choices.

witness.initial: Telegram-prepared facts suggest project P1 and visible=true; the operator intends project P2 and visible=false.
events: The operator publishes the prepared photo.
outcomes: The staff choices P2/hidden are authoritative.
The Telegram DTO choices P1/visible are authoritative, or the mismatch is rejected.
witness.observer: The operator and clients of P1/P2

open_points.subject: temporary-route intake identity minting
open_points.text: `intake_id` is a stable external identity owned by the intake boundary, but M34 also permits "the operator placing binaries until the intake service exists" without saying who mints `intake_id` on that temporary route.
open_points.question: Who creates the stable `intake_id` before the future intake service exists?
options: The operator or its local placement tool must generate it
The portal generates it when the photo is published
The temporary route cannot publish until an external intake ID exists
open_points.default_guess: Require the operator-side placement tool to generate and retain a stable intake ID.

witness.initial: The future intake service does not exist; an operator has placed a photo binary by the temporary route.
events: The operator publishes the photo.
The response is lost and the operator retries.
outcomes: A stable operator-generated intake ID makes the retry idempotent.
The portal generates a new ID on each attempt and may create duplicate photos.

open_points.subject: conflicting photo replay
open_points.text: The only replay rule is "replay of one `intake_id` never duplicates"; it does not say what happens when the same `intake_id` is submitted with different `file_ref`, project, date, section, caption, or visibility.
open_points.question: Does a conflicting replay return the existing ProgressPhoto unchanged, reject as an integrity conflict, or update it?
options: Reject differing content as an integrity conflict
Return the existing photo unchanged for every repeated intake ID
Treat mutable presentation fields as edits but reject changes to source identity facts
open_points.default_guess: Reject any differing creation content and require explicit edit actions for caption, section, or visibility.

witness.initial: Photo X exists for intake ID I with file F1 in project P.
events: Staff republishes I with file F2 and a different caption.
outcomes: The request is rejected and X remains unchanged.
The existing photo is returned unchanged or updated, depending on how replay is interpreted.
witness.observer: The publishing staff member and client

open_points.subject: hidden expense-document metadata in client reads
open_points.text: State 0 says the client reads "client-visible documents" and hidden reads are concealed, but `ExpenseView` always contains an `ExpenseDocumentView` with `client_visible`, without stating whether a hidden document is omitted, its metadata is still returned, or the entire expense is shaped differently.
open_points.question: What does a client-facing ExpenseView contain when the expense's sole document has `client_visible = false`?
options: The expense remains visible but its document field is absent or replaced by an explicit unavailable value
The hidden document metadata and `client_visible=false` are returned, while binary access is denied
The entire expense is omitted
open_points.default_guess: Keep the expense visible but omit the document projection and deny binary access without revealing why.

witness.initial: An included expense exists and staff changes its document to hidden.
events: A viewer reads the expense summary.
The viewer requests the document binary by its known ID.
outcomes: The expense remains in financial totals but the response reveals no hidden document metadata; binary access is concealed.
The ExpenseView still exposes the document ID and hidden flag, though the binary request is concealed.
